title: Integration tests: synthetic SLO breach triggers auto-rollback (latency + 5xx)
creator: Leila Farouk
links: Confluence: auto-rollback SLO integration design spec (draft)
GitHub: redwood PR-18529 (synthetic SLO breach integration tests)
GitHub: redwood PR-18546 (unknown verdict when monitor stale/unavailable)
Dashboards: Rollout SLO dashboards (latency + error) - staging
description:
Context
We’re adding automatic rollback when latency/error SLOs breach during model/version rollouts. We need an end-to-end harness that validates the full loop in a realistic environment:
1) rollout-controller reads monitors using the canonical monitor identity contract,
2) evaluator computes verdict using policy semantics (windows/min-traffic/cooldown/baseline/unknown handling),
3) rollback executor reverts traffic split to prior stable,
4) audit events + notifications are emitted.

Why this ticket
Unit tests cover evaluator logic, but we’ve repeatedly been burned by integration gaps (label mismatches, monitor staleness, query template changes, metrics pipeline delays). This harness is meant to catch “it works in code but won’t rollback in prod” failures before we enable auto-rollback for broader cohorts.

Goals
- Provide deterministic(ish) integration coverage for two breach modes:
  - latency regression (p95) breach
  - error-rate (5xx) breach
- Validate the complete rollback loop (monitor -> verdict -> executor -> traffic split) using real monitor API + telemetry pipeline in a staging environment.
- Define CI gating criteria and placement (PR-level vs merge-level vs nightly) with flake mitigation.

Non-goals
- Building a new monitoring system or new SLO tooling.
- Exhaustive policy semantics matrix testing (that belongs in evaluator unit/contract tests).
- Quality regressions (LLM output). Only latency/error SLOs.

Proposed approach (integration harness)
Test environment
- Run against the existing staging control plane + routing stack ("staging-us-west-2"), using an ephemeral namespace per CI run (e.g., rollout-e2e-$BUILD_ID).
- Create/ensure dedicated test route + model pair:
  - route: /v1/chat/completions (or an internal canary route) under a test tenant
  - model: a small, cheap model variant to keep tokens/cost low
  - stable version: v1
  - candidate version: v2

How we simulate breaches
A) Error breach
- Enable a fault injection knob in the candidate deployment to return 5xx at a high rate (e.g., 30–50%) for requests tagged to candidate.
- Options discussed:
  1) runtime-level fault injection flag (preferred for determinism; requires it already exists)
  2) HTTP proxy fault injector in front of inference worker (less invasive; can simulate 5xx + timeouts)

B) Latency breach
- Enable an artificial delay (e.g., +800ms) for candidate traffic only.
- Keep response successful to ensure the signal is “latency only,” not “error.”

Traffic generation
- Use internal loadgen (k6) to produce enough requests to satisfy minTraffic (policy default) while staying inside staging quotas.
- Ensure requests include required labels/headers for monitor identity (route/model/region/tier) and can be partitioned by version (stable vs candidate) via rollout traffic split.

Assertions (what we check)
- Monitor API returns data (not stale) for both latency and error monitors for the test identity.
- rollout-controller verdict transitions:
  - Healthy -> Breaching -> RollbackTriggered (or equivalent)
  - If monitor is stale/unavailable: verdict becomes Unknown and does NOT rollback (per guardrail PR-18546 / policy).
- Routing config is reverted:
  - candidate weight goes to 0%
  - stable returns to 100%
  - rollback is idempotent (re-running the executor doesn’t create drift)
- Audit events emitted:
  - AutoRollbackTriggered
  - RollbackExecuted
  - Includes monitor identity, policy id, rollout id, and actor="system"
- (Optional in this ticket; ok to defer) incident-bot notification is sent (we can assert on event stream payload or mocked sink, depending on staging capabilities).

CI gating plan
We need to balance coverage vs cost/flakiness:
1) PR-level (fast) contract tests
- Run with a FakeMonitorClient in-process.
- Verifies evaluator/executor integration and idempotency without relying on telemetry.
- Already largely covered elsewhere; this ticket adds a minimal "smoke" contract test that mirrors the e2e scenario.

2) Merge-to-main gate (medium)
- Run 1 scenario (error breach) end-to-end in staging with tightened timeouts and a small traffic target.
- Gate only the auto-rollback feature-flagged codepaths (skip when unrelated code changes to reduce noise).

3) Nightly (full)
- Run both scenarios (latency + error), plus one monitor-outage simulation.
- Persist artifacts: verdict trace logs, monitor query results, routing diff, and audit-event ids.

Flake mitigation
- Allow one retry at the harness level if the failure is due to known transient classes (monitor not ready, staging deploy delayed). If it fails twice, fail hard.
- Explicitly record “monitor lag” (time from injected fault to monitor breach observed) and alert if it trends above threshold; do not fail the test on single-run lag unless it exceeds a hard cap (e.g., 10 minutes).

Acceptance criteria
- A single command (CI job) can:
  1) deploy stable+candidate,
  2) start rollout with canary split,
  3) inject latency OR errors into candidate,
  4) generate traffic to exceed minTraffic,
  5) observe breach verdict,
  6) confirm rollback to stable,
  7) confirm audit events exist.
- Test runtime:
  - merge-gate scenario completes in <= 20 minutes
  - nightly full suite completes in <= 45 minutes
- Produces debuggable output on failure (links to rollout id, monitor identity, and last N evaluator traces).

Open questions
- What is the smallest evaluation window we can safely use in staging without changing global SLO tooling? (Proposed: 1m windows for e2e policy in test tenant only.)
- Do we have an approved fault injection mechanism in inference workers already, or do we need a proxy? If proxy, who owns deployment in staging?
- For alerting/notifications, should the e2e test assert on the event stream only (more reliable) vs Slack delivery (flaky)?

Implementation notes
- Prefer building the harness in the existing e2e test repo layout used by release engineering (so we get standard log capture + retries).
- The test tenant/policies should be created via API in setup, not by manual pre-provisioning, to prevent drift.

comments: 2025-01-29 (Sahana Iyer): Started a draft harness that provisions: test tenant -> rollout policy (1m window, minTraffic=200, cooldown=10m) -> stable/candidate versions. Blocked on having a deterministic fault injection mechanism for latency that doesn’t require rebuilding the model container each run.

2025-02-03 (Benji Okafor): For error injection, we can use the existing header-based "x-redwood-fault=force_5xx" in staging inference-gateway (added for load testing). For latency, there is a config knob in gateway to add fixed delay by route; I’ll confirm it can be scoped to candidate traffic only.

2025-02-05 (Miles Thornton): Please add a third case for monitor outage/staleness. We saw false rollbacks when monitor data went missing; we need to prove "Unknown" verdict does not rollback by default. Don’t rely on actually breaking Mimir; just stub monitor client to return stale timestamps in one e2e run if possible.

2025-02-07 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented initial assertions: traffic split revert + audit events lookup. Seeing occasional delay where monitor API reports data, but evaluator still sees "insufficient points". Adding explicit wait for monitor series to have >= 3 datapoints before starting canary.

2025-02-11 (Leila Farouk): Reviewed failure logs from 3 runs; main flake is rollout start racing metric label propagation. Suggest adding a warm-up phase: 2 minutes of baseline traffic to stable before shifting 10% to candidate, then begin fault injection.

2025-02-13 (Rafael Mendes): CI placement: +1 to nightly full suite; for merge-gate keep it to one scenario to reduce pager noise from staging. Also ensure the test posts a succinct summary to #eng-oncall-test-signal with rollout id + links when it fails, not paging.

2025-02-16 (Sahana Iyer): PR up with harness + CI job wiring (see PR-18529). Added warm-up, single retry, and artifact bundle (verdict trace + monitor query results + routing diff). Requesting review from Benji + Miles; next step is tighten timeouts and confirm cost/runtime meets criteria.
